question.text: Chenab Infrastructure Trust (Cat I-IIF) has set up an Investor Advisory Committee / advisory board. Which of the following BEST describes its typical governance role?

answer.text: The committee has binding investment-approval authority and replaces the Manager's Investment Committee
It is a SEBI-mandated committee that must include the Trustee as Chair
It functions as the external audit committee and signs off on annual financials

It is an optional Investor Advisory Committee / advisory board with a majority of investor representatives that acts as a check and balance, making recommendations to the Manager or the Investment Committee on matters such as conflicts of interest, risk management, governance, investor-manager relations, reporting and statutory/tax or administrative fund-document issues, without replacing the Manager/IC's investment-decision role

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes the Investor Advisory Committee (also called an advisory board) as an optional body, typically with a majority of investor representatives, that provides guidance and recommendations to the Manager or the Investment Committee. Its remit covers conflicts of interest, risk management, governance, investor-manager relations, reporting, statutory and tax matters and administrative fund-document issues. It serves a check-and-balance function rather than replacing the Manager or Investment Committee, which retains responsibility for investment proposals. The Trap: The "binding investment-approval authority" option confuses the advisory committee with the Manager / Investment Committee, which the workbook keeps separate. The "SEBI-mandated, Trustee-chair" option invents a composition the workbook does not prescribe; the body is set up contractually, not by regulation. The "external audit committee" option conflates the advisory role with statutory audit functions. Note: Read the workbook precisely: the advisory committee/board is optional, investor-majority, advisory in nature, and explicitly does not displace the Manager or Investment Committee in investment decision-making.
